newsitem.title: USA: Unocal Q4 earnings lifted by oil, gas prices.
newsitem.headline: Unocal Q4 earnings lifted by oil, gas prices.

text.p: Unocal Corp said Thursday its fourth quarter 1996 operating earnings got a boost from higher crude oil and natural gas prices in addition to increased foreign oil and gas production.
These operating gains were offset partially by increased depreciation and depletion expense, the company said.
The company's average worldwide natural gas sales price in the quarter was $2.49 per thousand cubic feet (mcf), up from $1.89 per mcf in 1995.
Average sales price for crude and condensate was $21.85, up from $15.07 last year.
Total revenues from continuing operations for the fourth quarter were $1.38 billion, up from $1.16 billion in the same period 1995.
For the full-year 1996, revenues from continuing operations were $5.33 billion, up from $4.39 billion the year before.
Earnings and revenues from continuing operations for 1996 and 1995 excluded the results of Unocal's 76 Products Company due to its pending sale.
"This was truly a breakthrough year for Unocal," said Roger Beach, Unocal chairman and chief executive officer.

"We recorded our strongest operating performance in many years from our upstream operations and made significant progress in realigning the company's assets so we can continue to grow for the future."

The agricultural products division's full-year earnings were $98 million, 40 percent above last year's results, the compnay said, attibuting the increase to higher sales volumes and record production levels.
